main.description: Assert a first-class AUTHORIZATION edge into the kotoba Datom log (:adauth.edge/*), parsed from the PUBLIC IAB web-standard files ads.txt / app-ads.txt / sellers.json. A publisher declares which seller may sell its inventory under an account-id as :direct or :reseller — the supply-chain backbone + the two-sided handshake. ads.txt / sellers.json are public files every publisher/exchange posts, so an edge is typically :authoritative. A DECLARED-but-not-CONFIRMED edge (declared && !confirmed) is the unauthorized / spoofed-inventory surface — sukashi's headline fraud-signal source. sukashi is an OBSERVATORY, NOT an ad network (G2).

publisher.description: :adtech/id of the PUBLISHER whose /ads.txt (or /app-ads.txt) this row came from

seller.description: :adtech/id of the ad-system / exchange domain (ads.txt field 1)

accountId.description: :adauth.edge/account-id — the publisher's account/seller id at the seller (ads.txt field 2)

relationship.description: :direct (publisher controls the account) | :reseller (an intermediary resells) — ads.txt field 3

certAuthority.description: :adauth.edge/cert-authority — TAG-ID / certification authority id (ads.txt field 4), if present

declared.description: true = the row is present in the publisher's ads.txt (its side of the handshake)

confirmed.description: true = a matching seller_id is present in the seller's sellers.json (the other side). declared && !confirmed = the unauthorized / spoofed-inventory surface

app.description: :adauth.edge/app — bundle id / store id when sourced from app-ads.txt (mobile/CTV), else absent

sourcing.description: ads.txt / sellers.json are public files → typically :authoritative (G5)
